question: What is the main reason we make special beds in the hospital?

options.A: To make the ward look neat for morning inspection
options.B: To ensure all beds in the ward look identical
options.C: To reduce the overall laundry workload of the hospital
options.D: To meet specific therapeutic and clinical needs of patients

explanation: You've got this! Special beds are designed and arranged specifically to support clinical care and keep patients safe based on their medical condition. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T3#BMP110_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why are special bed-making skills so important in our Nigerian healthcare wards?

options.A: They are required by law for every patient admitted to a private ward
options.B: They replace the need for regular vital sign monitoring
options.C: They eliminate the requirement for patient mobility altogether
options.D: They help prevent complications like pressure ulcers and respiratory distress

explanation: Great thinking! Properly arranged beds directly protect vulnerable patients from physical complications during their hospital stay. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T3#BMP110_U4_T3_h1)

question: Where should you put used hospital linen right after removing it from a bed?

options.A: Over the back of a nearby empty chair
options.B: Directly into a designated laundry hamper
options.C: On the floor beside the patient's bedside table
options.D: Tucked neatly under the bottom mattress

explanation: Spot on! Putting used linen straight into a hamper stops the spread of germs and keeps the ward environment clean and safe. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T3#BMP110_U4_T3_h2)

question: Why is it vital to smooth out all creases and wrinkles from the bottom sheet?

options.A: To ensure the bed looks aesthetically pleasing to visitors
options.B: To make it easier to tuck the sheet under the mattress
options.C: To prevent the mattress from absorbing body moisture
options.D: To prevent friction and the formation of pressure sores

explanation: You nailed it! Constant body weight plus wrinkles creates friction that breaks down delicate skin layers, leading to pressure sores. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T3#BMP110_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is another common name for the admission bed?
explanation: That's right! We call it an open or reception bed because it is kept ready for a new patient to settle in quickly and comfortably. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T3#BMP110_U4_T3_h3)

question: When preparing an admission bed for a new patient, how should you arrange the top covers?

options.A: Pulled tightly all the way to the head of the bed
options.B: Rolled tightly into a bolster shape at the center
options.C: Removed entirely and stored inside the bedside locker
options.D: Fan-folded to the side or bottom of the bed

explanation: Awesome! Fan-folding the covers makes it simple and fast for an incoming patient to slide right into bed. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T3#BMP110_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the main job of a mackintosh on an operation (surgical) bed?

options.A: To absorb excess sweat during a post-op fever
options.B: To keep the top bed sheets securely tucked in place
options.C: To protect the mattress from body fluids and drainage
options.D: To provide extra warmth for the recovering patient

explanation: Spot on! A mackintosh is a waterproof sheet that shields the mattress from blood, vomit, or other post-surgery fluids. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T3#BMP110_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why are the top covers fan-folded to one side on an operation bed?

options.A: To leave room for heavy woolen blankets on top
options.B: To make transferring the patient from a trolley quick and safe
options.C: To allow air to circulate freely under the patient's body
options.D: To ensure the nursing staff can change the sheets without waking them

explanation: You got it! Post-op patients come straight from a stretcher, so side-folding means you don't have to lift them over tangled blankets. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T3#BMP110_U4_T3_h4)

question: Which bed position is best when preparing a cardiac bed for a patient who is struggling to breathe?

options.B: Flat supine position with no pillows
options.D: Prone position with face turned to the side

explanation: Brilliant! Sitting upright pulls the diaphragm down, making it much easier for the lungs to expand and easing the strain on the heart. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T3#BMP110_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why do we place extra pillows under the arms of a patient in a cardiac bed?

options.A: To ensure the patient stays fast asleep during the night
options.B: To prevent the development of wrist drop contractures
options.C: To keep the IV cannula safe from accidental pulling
options.D: To support the arms and reduce respiratory effort

explanation: That's correct! Supporting the arms lifts their weight off the chest, helping the breathing muscles work with much less fatigue. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T3#BMP110_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which bed-making mistake spreads dust and germs all over the ward air?

options.A: Placing wet mackintoshes directly into a laundry bag
options.B: Rolling the dirty linen inward toward the center
options.C: Holding soiled linen away from the nurse's uniform
options.D: Shaking or snapping bed sheets in the air

explanation: You've got this! Never shake or snap sheets—it flings dust, skin flakes, and bacteria into the air for everyone to breathe in. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T3#BMP110_U4_T3_h6)

question: How should you carry dirty bed linen so it doesn't contaminate your uniform?

options.A: Away from the body, holding it clear of the uniform
options.B: Draped loosely over both shoulders like a shawl
options.C: Tucked securely right against the front of the apron
options.D: Balanced on top of the head while walking quickly

explanation: Spot on! Always keep used linen away from your clothes so germs don't hitch a ride to your next patient. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T3#BMP110_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which of these details is least important to chart after making a special bed?

options.A: The brand name of the mattress used on the bed
options.B: The specific type of special bed prepared for the patient
options.C: Any relevant observations regarding patient comfort or skin
options.D: The exact time the bed procedure was completed

explanation: Great clinical intuition! The mattress brand doesn't matter for charting, but knowing the bed type, time, and patient comfort is essential. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T3#BMP110_U4_T3_h7)

question: Why should you quickly check on your patient right after settling them into a new special bed?

options.A: To see if the patient is ready to be discharged home
options.B: To fulfill a legal requirement for writing the night report
options.C: To check if the laundry department sent enough clean pillowcases
options.D: To confirm that the positioning and bed setup meet their clinical needs

explanation: You got it! A quick check ensures the patient is safe, comfortable, and properly supported by your special bed setup. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T3#BMP110_U4_T3_h7)
